subject: Clarify: transient cache replication & data residency commitments
messages:
From: Elena Martin <dpo@acme.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>
Cc: Josh Patel <legal@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Mar 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Question on caching behavior and cross-region replication

Hi Marcus / Laura,

Quick question from Acme's privacy team as we review the DPA redline: the technical appendix references that Redwood may use caching and batching to improve latency. Can you confirm whether the KV/prefix caches or any ephemeral inference caches may ever be replicated or checkpointed to a different region than the one we pin? For our EU-only requirement we need assurance that user content will not be copied to non-EU regions except for a small set of infra operations.

Specifically:
- Are prefix/KV caches stored durably or transiently?
- If a cache shard is warm in eu-west1 and traffic shifts, could it be replicated to a us region for failover or burst?
- Do any subprocessors (CDN, metrics, caching) have access to replicated cache blobs?

We need precise language so our legal team can sign off on the redline. If helpful, happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Martin
DPO, Acme Corp
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>
To: Elena Martin <dpo@acme.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example>
Date: Sat, 07 Mar 2026 13:03:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Question on caching behavior and cross-region replication

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear questions. Short answer up front: persistent user content is not copied to non-EU persistent storage under our EU pinning option; however, there are limited, documented cases where transient inference artifacts (ephemeral KV/prefix caches used to serve low-latency requests) may be replicated for short windows during failover or burst, and we can commit to strict controls and logging around that.

Details:
- Nature of caches: our prefix/KV caches are in-memory optimized shards by default (not written to durable block storage). We treat them as ephemeral working state used to accelerate token generation.
- Replication behaviour: by default caches stay in-region. For Dedicated/Private customers we offer region locking (no cross-region replication). For Hosted customers with EU pin enabled, we route primary writes/ingest to EU. However, in extreme scenarios (regional outage or rapid traffic spike where a warm cache is required to meet latency SLOs) our automatic failover may briefly spin up workers in a nearby compatible region. When that happens we may replicate only the minimal, anonymized cache metadata necessary to continue the request.
- Time window: such replicated artifacts are retained only for the duration of the single failover/burst session (typically seconds to a few minutes) and are not persisted to long-term storage.
- Subprocessors: we do use third-party infra partners for metrics and autoscaling orchestration. Those partners do not receive the cache contents; they receive aggregated telemetry. We can provide an up-to-date subprocessors list.

Next steps I propose:
1) We can provide a concise DPA clause that captures the above and calls out the short retention window and logging/fall-back policy.
2) We will attach our current subprocessors export and a link to the latest SOC2 Type II report.
3) If you need tighter controls, our Dedicated and Private deployment options can be contracted to guarantee no cross-region worker starts (we can capture as a contractual obligation).

I'm attaching a short tech note and will follow up with a DPA paragraph suggestion. If you prefer a call, I can bring Soojin (product security) and Neha (privacy) next week.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Question on caching behavior and cross-region replication — suggested DPA language

Team — below is Elena's ask. Drafting a DPA paragraph we can propose; please review and suggest edits (especially legal & security notes):

Draft paragraph (to include in Annex A - Data Handling):
"Redwood Inference will process Customer Data in the EU region(s) designated by Customer for the duration of the Services. Transient in-memory inference artifacts (including KV/prefix caches and other ephemeral runtime state) are treated as non-persistent operational artifacts. Redwood will not write or persist Customer Data to durable storage outside the designated EU region except: (a) during temporary failover or burst scenarios where a compatible non-EU region is required to maintain Service availability; and (b) if Customer explicitly requests cross-region processing. Any transient replication under (a) will be limited to the minimum runtime state required to continue the specific request, retained only for the duration of the failover session, and logged to Customer-accessible audit records. Redwood will provide an up-to-date list of subprocessors and SOC 2 Type II evidence upon request."
Questions for review:
- Soojin: is the "minimum runtime state" wording accurate and defensible? Any security caveats we should add?
- Neha: does the logging/audit sentence map to our current event retention and export capabilities?
- Laura: commercial note — if Acme wants an absolute prohibition (no cross-region warm starts), we should price Dedicated as an explicit add-on and propose contract language.

Attachments: technical note summary (for Elena) + subprocessors CSV (current). I will not attach SOC2 here; we'll provide the Drive link per standard NDA.

-Marcus
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>
To: Elena Martin <dpo@acme.com>, Josh Patel <legal@acme.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on caching behavior and cross-region replication — proposed commitments and next steps

Hi Elena / Josh — follow-up with the artifacts we promised.

Summary & commitments:
- Persistent Customer Data: will remain stored only in the customer-designated EU region(s) unless Customer explicitly requests otherwise.
- Transient artifacts: KV/prefix caches and ephemeral runtime state are non-persistent. In Hosted EU-pin mode these artifacts are not replicated to non-EU regions under normal operation. In an automated failover or emergency burst, Redwood may temporarily instantiate compatible workers outside the EU; any replicated runtime state will be limited to the minimum necessary for request continuity, retained only for the session, and subsequently discarded.
- Auditability: Redwood will log any cross-region execution events and make those events available via the Console audit feed and as downloadable records for the period covered by your contract.
- Subprocessors & evidence: attached is our current subprocessors export (redwood_subprocessors_list_20260310.csv). SOC2 Type II report is available at the link: https://drive.redwood.example/reports/soc2-2025-type2 (we can share a signed copy under NDA).

Proposed contract language (same as the draft Marcus circulated internally) is attached as a PDF (ACME_DPA_redline_request.pdf) — we limited the wording to the narrow exception described above. If you require absolute region immutability (no possibility of cross-region warm starts), we can support that for Dedicated/Private with a contractual commitment; I'll ask Laura to provide a quote and amendment path.

Next steps:
- Elena / Josh: please review the attached paragraph and subprocessors list and let us know if that addresses Acme's legal concerns.
- If useful, we can schedule a 30-minute technical Q&A next week (Soojin + Neha attending).

Thanks,
Marcus
Attachments: ACME_DPA_redline_request.pdf (draft clause), redwood_subprocessors_list_20260310.csv, soc2-type2-link.txt
